title: Osiris and Set (Egyptian mythology)
subtitle: Egyptian mythology
subject: mythologie
description: Murder, dismemberment, mummy and revenge: the cycle of Osiris and Set founded Egyptian royalty and the hope of life after death.

hero.hook: A brother kills the king, cuts his body into fourteen pieces. A sister brings him together. A son avenges. The whole of Egypt is emerging from this crime.

blocks.text: The cycle of **Osiris** and **Set** is the great story of ancient Egypt. This is not just a family tragedy. It is the fight between order (, harmony) and sterile chaos. [[Ma'at]]

Through the murder, dismemberment and resurrection of Osiris, the Egyptians think about kingship, the fertility of the Nile and life after death. Every living pharaoh is a **Horus**. Each dead king becomes a **Osiris**.

**Osiris** is a civilizing king. With his sister-wife **Isis**, he teaches agriculture and laws. His brother **Set**, god of the desert and violence, hates him. At a banquet, Set presents a magnificent chest: he will offer it to the one who fits it perfectly.

blocks.caption: Osiris with green skin: not death, but vegetation reborn.

blocks.text: Having taken Osiris's measurements in secret, Set makes him lie down, locks the chest, seals it with lead and throws him into the Nile. Later, when Isis finds the body, Set cuts it into **14 pieces** and scatters them throughout the valley. Without an intact body, there is no peace in the afterlife.
Osiris is often painted green. This color does not say rot: it says rebirth, like the fields after the Nile floods.

**Isis**, great magician, sets out in search of the fragments. Helped by her sister Nephthys and the god , she erects a sanctuary in each place where she finds a piece. One problem remains: the phallus was devoured by the fish . Isis fashions a replacement. [[Anubis]] [[Oxyrhynchus]]

blocks.caption: Isis with outstretched wings: the breath that revives Osiris.

blocks.text: By gathering the pieces and wrapping them in strips, Isis and Anubis create the first **mummy**. With a beat of her wings, Isis breathed brief life into Osiris. It was then that she conceived **Horus**, the heir destined to restore order.
According to some texts, the tears of Isis during her quest were so abundant that the Egyptians saw in them the mythical origin of the annual flood of the Nile.

Raise[[D]] in secret in the swamps of , **Horus** grows into the form of the hawk. As an adult, he claims the throne before the tribunal of the gods, presided over by . The conflict with Set lasts decades: duels, tricks, injuries. Horus loses an eye; Set loses his fertility. [[Khemmis]]

blocks.caption: The Eye of Horus (Oudjat): integrity regained from chaos.

blocks.text: The eye, recomposed by , becomes the symbol of healing and protection. The gods decide: Set is condemned to serve, notably by fighting the serpent  on the solar boat. Horus is crowned. Every pharaoh will henceforth be a “living Horus”. [[Thoth]] [[Apophis]]

Mummified, Osiris can no longer reign on earth. He becomes ruler of the **Amenti**, the kingdom of the dead. Under his gaze, the **weighing of the heart**, described in , takes place. The heart of the deceased is placed on a scale facing the feather of Ma'at. [[The Book of the Dead]]

If the heart is light, the deceased is “right in voice” and enters the eternity of Osiris. If it is full of mistakes, the [[Ammout]] monster devours it: definitive oblivion. King and peasant are judged according to the same criteria. Horus manages the present; Osiris takes care of the rest.

The myth of **Osiris** and **Set** establishes three pillars of Egypt: royalty (living Horus), mummification (intact body for the afterlife) and the hope of justice after death under the gaze of Osiris.
